## Materials and methods

CCC-RISE infers cell--cell communication (CCC) programs across multiple conditions in three sequential steps, illustrated in Fig. 1: (1) RISE decomposes the multi-condition scRNA-seq data into cell eigen-states; (2) an aligned 4D communication tensor is constructed by scoring ligand--receptor pairs between eigen-states; and (3) CPD decomposes this tensor to extract communication programs.
Each step is described in turn below, followed by the data processing, rank selection, validation, and interpretation analyses.

### Reduction and Insight in Single-cell Exploration

Reduction and Insight in Single-cell Exploration (RISE) is a computational framework based on the PARAFAC2 tensor decomposition method, optimized for analyzing multi-condition scRNA-seq data\ [@doi:10.1016/j.cels.2025.101294].
A major challenge in scRNA-seq is that the data lacks alignment when reconstructed into a 3D tensor, because the same cell is not measured across conditions.
RISE overcomes this by using the PARAFAC2 model, which solves for the alignment of the data along one dimension---the cell axis.
The input to RISE, $X_{\mathrm{sc},i} \in \mathbb{R}^{J_{\mathrm{sc},i} \times K}$, is the normalized expression (see Data Processing) of the $J_{\mathrm{sc},i}$ cells of condition $i = 1, \ldots, I$ over $K$ genes, centered on $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^{K}$, the per-gene mean over all cells of all conditions.
In fitting the RISE model, we seek:

$$
  \underset{A,C,\mathbf{P}}{\operatorname{argmin}}\sum_{i=1}^{I}w_{i}^{2}\left\| X_{\mathrm{sc},i} - P_{i}\operatorname{diag}\left( a_{i} \right)C^{T} \right\|^{2}\text{subject to}\ {P_{i}}^{T}P_{i}\mathbf{\ } = \mathbf{I\ \forall\ }i
$$

where $w_{i}$ are the slice weights (see below); $\mathbf{P =}P_{i} \in \mathbb{R}^{J_{\mathrm{sc},i} \times r},\ \ i\  = \ 1,\ 2,\ \ldots,\ I$ are the projection matrices and $r$ is the rank of the RISE decomposition; $\operatorname{diag}\left( a_{i} \right)$ is the diagonal matrix whose nonzero entries are equal to the $i$^th^ row of $A \in \mathbb{R}^{I \times r}$, the condition factor matrix; $C \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times r}$ is the gene factor matrix; and $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity matrix\ [@doi:10/cxfskg].
The general PARAFAC2 model includes a third factor matrix, $B \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times r}$, between $P_{i}$ and $\operatorname{diag}\left( a_{i} \right)$; CCC-RISE fixes $B = \mathbf{I}$, so each condition's eigen-state coordinates are the orthonormal columns of $P_{i}$.
The $r$ cell eigen-states are therefore defined jointly by the projections and the gene factor: eigen-state $q$ has gene profile $c_{q}$, scaled by $a_{iq}$ in condition $i$, and column $q$ of $P_{i}$ gives each cell's projection onto the shared gene expression factors.

**Slice normalization.** Conditions differ in cell number and total variance, so without weighting, conditions with many or highly variable cells would dominate the fit.
Each condition was therefore weighted by the inverse of its mean-centered Frobenius norm, $w_{i} = 1/\left\| X_{\mathrm{sc},i} \right\|_{F}$, during fitting so that every sample contributed equally to the objective.
Equivalently, RISE was fit to the weighted slices $w_{i}X_{\mathrm{sc},i}$, and each row of $A$ was divided by $w_{i}$ after fitting so that the factors reconstructed the unweighted data.

**Fitting.** In fitting RISE, we obtained $\mathbf{P}$ and the factor matrices $A$ and $C$.
First, for fixed projections, the factor matrices were updated as:

$$
  \underset{A,C}{\operatorname{argmin}}\sum_{i=1}^{I}w_{i}^{2}\left\| X_{\mathrm{sc},i} - P_{i}\operatorname{diag}\left( a_{i} \right)C^{T} \right\|^{2}
$$

$$
  = \underset{A,C}{\operatorname{argmin}}\sum_{i=1}^{I}\left\| w_{i}P_{i}^{T}X_{\mathrm{sc},i} - \operatorname{diag}\left( a_{i} \right)C^{T} \right\|^{2}
$$

which is equivalent to one alternating least-squares (ALS) update of $A$ and $C$ in a PARAFAC model of the aligned third-order tensor whose $i$^th^ slice along the first mode is $w_{i}P_{i}^{T}X_{\mathrm{sc},i}$, with the eigen-state factor fixed to the identity.
Then, the projection matrices, $\mathbf{P,}$ were updated by solving the Orthogonal Procrustes problem.
Given matrices $M,N \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}$, the Orthogonal Procrustes problem seeks an orthogonal matrix $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ that minimizes $\left\| MQ - N \right\|_{F}^{2}$.
The solution is given by $Q = UV^{T}$, where $U\Sigma V^{T}$ is the singular value decomposition of $N^{T}M$.
For a low-rank decomposition, we updated each $P_{i} \in \mathbf{P}$ as $P_{i} = UV^{T}$, the product of the $r$ left and right singular vectors from the thin SVD $U\Sigma V^{T}$ of $X_{\mathrm{sc},i}C\,\operatorname{diag}\left( a_{i} \right)$.
This cycle of aligning the tensor and then factoring it was repeated until the decrease in the weighted relative squared error, $\sum_{i}w_{i}^{2}\left\| X_{\mathrm{sc},i} - P_{i}\operatorname{diag}\left( a_{i} \right)C^{T} \right\|^{2} / \sum_{i}w_{i}^{2}\left\| X_{\mathrm{sc},i} \right\|^{2}$, between iterations fell below 1×10^-8^, or until 300 iterations elapsed.

RISE enhances the core PARAFAC2 algorithm with key optimizations: $A$ was initialized to ones, $C$ was initialized to the leading $r$ right singular vectors of the stacked, centered, and slice-weighted data, (computed with an iterative (LOBPCG) eigensolver from a random start), and fitted components were ordered by the variance-to-mean ratio of their condition loadings, normalized, and sign-flipped to a consistent orientation\ [@doi:10.1016/j.cels.2025.101294; @doi:10.1137/S1064827500366124; @doi:10/cxfskg; @doi:10.1016/j.chemolab.2021.104312].

**CANDELINC compression.** Analyses requiring many RISE fits (bi-cross-validation, jackknife, and re-initialization, below) used CANDELINC compression\ [@doi:{10.1016/S0169-7439(98)00011-2}].
During compressed fits, the gene space was restricted to an orthonormal basis of the leading $L = \max(2r, r + 20)$ right singular vectors of the stacked, centered, and slice-weighted data, computed with LOBPCG for 20 iterations.
Each projected condition slice was further truncated to its leading $L$ left singular vectors, and RISE was fit to these compressed slices.
Compressed fits reduced the gene expression space, but yielded nearly identical components to uncompressed fits.
All RISE fits besides those used for bi-cross-validation, jackknife, and re-initialization testing were uncompressed.

**Visualization.** PaCMAP was applied to the RISE projections of all cells concatenated across conditions, with default parameters, to visualize cell-to-cell variation as an embedding\ [@arxiv:2012.04456].

### Construction of the Aligned 4D Communication Tensor

From the eigen-state factors that RISE produces, CCC scores were calculated for all relevant LR pairs in each experimental condition, with each pair of eigen-states as sender and receiver.
LR pairs were obtained from the human CellChatDB resource of 2,005 annotated interactions, including multimeric complexes\ [@doi:10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9].
Pairs were retained only if every ligand and receptor subunit gene was present in the expression data.
The expression of a multimeric complex was taken as the minimum expression of its subunits.
The expression of eigen-state $q$ in condition $i$ is the corresponding row of $P_{i}^{T}X_{\mathrm{sc},i} + \mathbf{1}\mu^{T}$, clipped at 0, where $\mu$ is the per-gene mean that RISE centers on (above).

**CCC scoring.** To model CCC, we represented the expression of a ligand and its receptor as the outer product of the gene expression for a LR pair.
This operation captures the combinatorial potential for signaling, where each element in the resulting matrix represents the product of a sender eigen-state's ligand expression and a receiver eigen-state's receptor expression.
In doing so, we assumed the LR interactions were proportional to the mRNA abundance of the ligand and receptor.
When extended across all LR pairs and conditions, these formed an aligned 4D communication tensor with dimensions of condition, sender eigen-state, receiver eigen-state, and LR pair.
The tensor was assembled with the code developed for Tensor-cell2cell\ [@doi:10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2].

**Sign convention for the communication score.** RISE eigen-state gene loadings are estimated relative to a fixed per-gene mean computed once over the full dataset ($\mu$), and subtracted off during the RISE fitting process.
The loadings are therefore a deviation from $\mu$, $\Delta$, and can be negative even though real expression is strictly non-negative.
Taking the outer product directly on two such deviations, $\Delta_L \Delta_R$, is only the interaction term of the full expansion of actual expression, $(\mu_L + \Delta_L)(\mu_R + \Delta_R) = \mu_L\mu_R + \mu_L\Delta_R + \mu_R\Delta_L + \Delta_L\Delta_R$; discarding the baseline and both main-effect terms lets two negative deviations produce a spuriously large positive score indistinguishable from two positive ones.
We therefore added $\mu$ back to each eigen-state's ligand/receptor loading before scoring, so the communication score approximates actual non-negative expression rather than a product of centered loadings.

**Alternative scoring functions.** Beyond the expression product used for the reported results, we implemented three alternative ways to combine a sender eigen-state's non-negative ligand expression, $L$, with a receiver eigen-state's non-negative receptor expression, $R$, into a communication score to assess robustness to this choice: an arithmetic mean, $(L + R)/2$, used by Tensor-cell2cell and CellPhoneDB; a geometric mean, $\sqrt{LR}$, used by scDiffCom; and a CellChat-style saturating Hill function, $LR / (K_h + LR)$, where $K_h = 0.5$ is a half-saturation constant\ [@doi:10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2; @doi:10.1038/s41596-020-0292-x; @doi:10.1038/s43587-023-00514-x; @doi:10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9].
All three require non-negative $L, R$, which our sign-convention correction above provides.

### Canonical Polyadic Decomposition

Canonical Polyadic Decomposition (CPD) was applied to the 4D communication tensor, resulting in factor matrices that explain the component associations with each of the four dimensions (conditions, sender eigen-states, receiver eigen-states, and LR pairs).
CPD is a tensor decomposition method that generalizes PCA to higher-order data structures, called tensors.
Given a third-order tensor, $\mathbf{X}$, of shape $I \times J \times K$, CPD seeks to approximate $\mathbf{X}$ as a sum of component rank-one tensors.
This set of component rank-one tensors are collectively represented in factor matrices: $A$ of shape $I \times r$, $B$ of shape $J \times r$, and $C$ of shape $K \times r$, where $r$ is the number of components into which $\mathbf{X}$ is decomposed.
Specifically, CPD seeks

$$
  \underset{A,B,C}{\operatorname{argmin}}\sum_{i=1}^{I}\left\| X_{i} - B\operatorname{diag}\left( a_{i} \right)C^{T} \right\|^{2}
$$

where $X_{\mathbf{i}}$ is the $i$^th^ slice of $\mathbf{X}$ along the first mode, and $\operatorname{diag}\left( a_{i} \right)$ is the diagonal matrix whose nonzero entries are equal to the $i$^th^ row of $A$.
The same model extends to the four modes of the communication tensor, yielding the condition ($D$), sender eigen-state ($E$), receiver eigen-state ($F$), and LR pair ($G$) factor matrices.

**Fitting.** While many algorithms exist for deriving CPD, we applied alternating least squares (ALS), wherein each mode is iteratively solved using least squares.
ALS stopped when the change in relative reconstruction error between iterations fell below 1×10^-12^, or after a maximum of 4,000 iterations.
As an iterative procedure, ALS must be initialized with a starting estimate of the factorization.
Each factor matrix was initialized with the leading $r$ left singular vectors of the corresponding mode unfolding of the tensor, computed by randomized SVD, and the factors were normalized to unit norm at each iteration, with their scale carried by a weight per component.

**Post-fit standardization.** CPD components are determined only up to order, scale, and sign, so each fit was standardized before interpretation.
Components were ordered by the variance-to-mean ratio of their condition factor ($D$) loadings, in ascending order, and every factor column was normalized to unit norm.
Signs were then flipped so that the condition, receiver eigen-state, and LR pair factors had positive column means; each flip was matched by a flip of the corresponding sender eigen-state column, leaving the component unchanged, so only sender signs are not directly interpretable.

**Total-expression correction.** Condition loadings scale with each sample's total normalized expression, the sum of normalized expression over all of the sample's cells.
Because sequencing depth was removed by per-cell normalization, this total was dominated by the number of cells per sample, not by read depth.
For each set of condition loadings, the norm of each sample's loading row was regressed on the sample's total normalized expression by ordinary least squares with an intercept, and each row was divided by its fitted value.

### Data Processing

**ALAD cohort.** The single-cell gene expression and clinical annotations of bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) samples were obtained from Calabrese et al.\ [@doi:10.1016/j.healun.2024.02.007].
Cells with 10 or fewer total counts and genes with a mean raw count of 0.001 or less across all cells were removed.
Each cell was scaled to the median per-cell total count, and each gene was then scaled by its sum across cells.
The data were then log-transformed as

$$
  g(x) = \log_{10}\left( 1 + 1000x \right)
$$

where $x$ is the scaled expression and $g(x)$ the transformed expression.
Finally, each gene was centered on its mean, $\mu$, which RISE subtracts internally.
The final dataset consisted of 51,273 cells and 16,675 genes.
After filtering the CellChatDB list of interacting LR pairs to the genes in the dataset, 513 LR pairs were retained.
The uncompressed data were fit with a 17-component RISE model and a 5-component CPD model, selected as described in Rank Selection.

**IBD cohort.** The single-cell gene expression, cell-type annotations, and biopsy metadata of terminal-ileum pinch biopsies were obtained from the IBDverse atlas of Krzak et al.: 343 biopsies, one per individual, from 232 healthy participants and 111 patients with Crohn's disease (CD), 47 uninflamed and 64 inflamed\ [@doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02634-7].
We excluded the mesenchymal lineage (fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and pericytes; 11,286 of 1,185,861 cells), because the authors attribute its underrepresentation in the atlas to the pinch biopsies and the digestive enzymes, which favor capturing epithelial cells; its yield accordingly varied across biopsies, from none to 11% of a biopsy's cells, independently of inflammation status (Kruskal--Wallis p = 0.14).
This left 7 lineages (coarse labels) and 54 annotated cell types (fine labels).
Cells and genes were filtered and normalized as for ALAD, with the gene filter measured on all remaining cells, and mitochondrial and ribosomal genes were also removed.
To fit in memory, each biopsy was capped at 2,000 cells drawn at random from the cells passing the count filter, which subsampled 245 of the 343 biopsies and kept 634,534 of 1,174,575 cells.
The cap kept the composition of each biopsy: within each subsampled biopsy, no lineage's share changed by more than 2.5%, and every lineage and cell type remained.
The final dataset consisted of 634,534 cells and 23,355 genes, with 1,255 LR pairs retained, and was fit with a 60-component RISE model and a 6-component CPD model, selected as described in Rank Selection.

### Fit Evaluation

Reconstruction error, R^2^X, or the fraction of variance explained by the model, was used to evaluate the effectiveness of the data reduction.
For RISE, the Frobenius norm of the difference between the scRNA-seq data ($X_{\mathrm{sc}}$) and the reconstruction from the RISE factors and projections ($X_{\mathrm{RISE}}$) was calculated.
This difference was normalized by the Frobenius norm of the data and subtracted from 1.

$$
  R^{2}X = 1 - \ \frac{\lVert X_{\mathrm{sc}} - X_{\mathrm{RISE}} \rVert^{2}}{\lVert X_{\mathrm{sc}} \rVert^{2}}
$$

For CPD, the Frobenius norm of the difference between the 4D communication tensor after CCC scoring ($X_{\mathrm{CCC\ 4D\ Tensor}}$) and the reconstruction from the CPD factors ($X_{\mathrm{CPD}}$) was calculated.
This difference was normalized by the Frobenius norm of the data and subtracted from 1:

$$
  R^{2}X = 1 - \ \frac{\lVert X_{\mathrm{CCC\ 4D\ Tensor}} - X_{\mathrm{CPD}} \rVert^{2}}{\lVert X_{\mathrm{CCC\ 4D\ Tensor}} \rVert^{2}}
$$

R^2^X ranges from 0 to 1, with a score of 1 indicating a perfect reconstruction.
The reported R^2^X was the unweighted reconstruction error, although the RISE fit used patient slice normalization.

The similarity of two factor columns, $u$ and $v$, was measured by their cosine similarity,

$$
  \cos\left( u,v \right) = \frac{u^{T}v}{\left\| u \right\|\left\| v \right\|}
$$

which ranges from −1 to 1 and is independent of the columns' scale, which CPD and RISE leave undetermined.
Because a column's sign is also undetermined, comparisons used the absolute cosine, $\left| \cos\left( u,v \right) \right|$, unless stated otherwise.

Factor match score (FMS) was used to evaluate the stability of the RISE and CPD factorizations\ [@doi:10.1137/21m1450033].
For a pair of factorizations, the FMS of component $q$ is the product, over the compared modes $m$, of the absolute cosine similarity between the two fits' factor columns,

$$
  {FMS}_{q} = \prod_{m}\left| \cos\left( M_{q}^{(m)},\widehat{M_{q}^{(m)}} \right) \right|
$$

where $M^{(m)}$ and $\widehat{M^{(m)}}$ are the reference and replicate factor matrices of mode $m$; component weights are not compared.
Replicate components were matched to the reference by Hungarian matching.
The aggregate FMS of a replicate is its mean FMS over components.

### Rank Selection

**RISE.** The RISE rank was selected by bi-cross-validation (BiCV)\ [@doi:10.1214/08-AOAS227].
In each repeat, 50% of the cells within each condition and 50% of the genes were held out, and RISE was fit to the training cells and training genes.
The held-out genes' loadings were estimated by least squares from the training cells' expression of those genes, and the held-out cells were projected onto the fit's eigen-states using the training genes.
The held-out R^2^X was then computed on the block of held-out cells and held-out genes.
This was repeated 10 times for each rank, using compressed RISE fits.
For ALAD, ranks 1 to 50 were tested and we selected the rank maximizing the mean held-out R^2^X.
For IBD, ranks 30 to 90 were tested in steps of 5; mean held-out R^2^X plateaued without a clear maximum, so we selected the smallest rank whose mean was within one standard error of the largest (rank 85), rank 60.

**CPD.** CPD ranks from 1 to the selected RISE rank were evaluated on the communication tensor from the uncompressed RISE fit.
At each rank, CPD was fit from 10 seeded starts of the same SVD initialization used for the reported fit (randomized SVD, seeds 42--51), in single precision on a GPU.
First, the fit R^2^X of each start was computed.
Second, the masked imputation R^2^X was computed, as follows.
Tensor entries were split into 10 random folds, so that every entry was held out once.
For each fold, the held-out entries were set to zero and the CPD model was fit by masked ALS, which iteratively fills the held-out entries with the current reconstruction.
The predictions of all held-out entries were pooled into a single R^2^X against the full tensor, and this was averaged over 10 repeated fold splits.
Imputation fits ran in double precision, because single-precision masked fits diverged at higher ranks.
A ridge penalty ($\lambda$ = 0.1) was applied to the masked fits only, because the communication tensor is heavy-tailed so an unpenalized masked fit could be dominated by the few largest held-out entries.
Third, the collinearity of each fit was measured in each mode as the largest absolute cosine between the factor columns of two of its components.
Fourth, the agreement between starts was measured by the FMS between every pair of a rank's starts.
Distinct minima were defined as groups of starts with FMS ≥ 0.95.
The rank was chosen as the largest rank at which no start's LR pair mode was collinear.

### Clinical Association Testing

Associations between components and outcomes were tested with the sample as the unit of analysis, using the corrected CPD condition loadings ($D$).
For ALAD, we tested nine groupings of samples: ALAD status (control vs. ALAD; control, declined, and recovered); six-month outcome (stable, recovered, CLAD, and died; CLAD vs. stable/recovered, excluding deaths; and died vs. alive); one-year outcome (stable, recovered, CLAD, and died; CLAD vs. no CLAD; and died vs. alive); and acute rejection (yes vs. no).
For IBD, we tested three groupings of biopsies by inflammation status: healthy, CD uninflamed, and CD inflamed; healthy vs. CD, pooling uninflamed and inflamed CD biopsies; and CD uninflamed vs. inflamed, excluding healthy biopsies.
For each component and grouping, we reported the one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) F statistic and effect size, $\eta^{2} = SS_{\mathrm{between}}/SS_{\mathrm{total}}$, with p-values corrected across all component by outcome tests.
For ALAD, RISE condition loadings ($A$) were corrected and tested in the same way, with correction across all RISE component by outcome tests.

Covariates were screened against each grouping by the same ANOVA, without the total-expression correction or multiple-testing correction, with binary covariates coded 0/1.
For ALAD, these were six patient covariates: age (years), sex, Caucasian ethnicity, an interstitial lung disease (ILD) transplant diagnosis, cytomegalovirus (CMV) IgG seropositivity, and baseline forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1).
For IBD, these were patient covariates (age, recorded in 10-year bins, and sex), sample covariates (10x Genomics chip version, B vs. G, and total sample expression), and cell-type covariates (the fraction of each biopsy's cells in each of the 7 lineages, after the 2,000-cell cap); the 6 biopsies without a recorded chip version were left out of its tests.

**Individual LR pair associations.** For each CPD component, each LR pair's communication score in each sample was computed as the sample's tensor slice for that pair weighted by the component's sender ($E$) and receiver ($F$) eigen-state loadings and summed, $S_{l,i} = \sum_{s,t} X_{l,s,t,i}e_{s}f_{t}$, where $X_{l,s,t,i}$ is the communication score of LR pair $l$ from sender eigen-state $s$ to receiver eigen-state $t$ in condition $i$.
These scores were corrected for total sample expression as above and tested against outcome by one-way ANOVA, with correction across the 513 LR pairs.
For the component's top 10 LR pairs by absolute LR pair loading, we computed the Spearman correlation of the uncorrected scores across samples between each pair of LR pairs.
LR pairs sharing a ligand or receptor gene, which co-vary in part by construction, were first merged into one by averaging their per-sample score ranks, directly or through another shared pair, both among the top LR pairs and within each baseline draw.
These correlations were compared with those of LR pairs drawn 2,000 times from three baselines: random LR pairs; expression-matched LR pairs, each drawn from the 20 LR pairs nearest a top pair in log mean score; and the other LR pairs associated with outcome (q < 0.05).

### Robustness Tests

**Patient jackknife.** Each patient was left out in turn, with both samples of a two-sample patient left out together, and each replicate was refit end to end at the selected ranks using compressed RISE fits and uncompressed, single-precision CPD fits.
Replicates were compared with a reference fit on the full data with the same settings by Hungarian matching and FMS.
Because the condition roster changed between replicates, RISE was compared on the gene mode only and CPD on the LR pair mode only; eigen-state modes were never compared.
To assess the stability of component--outcome associations, the ANOVA for an outcome grouping was repeated on each replicate's corrected CPD condition loadings, corrected for multiple testing across the components of that fit, and assigned to the matched reference component.

**Model re-initialization.** The full data were refit end to end with different random seeds, using the same fits and reference as above.
Because the conditions were unchanged, RISE was compared on the condition and gene modes and CPD on the condition and LR pair modes.

**Alternative CCC scoring** To assess robustness to the communication score, the communication tensor was recomputed from a single shared, uncompressed RISE fit under each alternative scoring function, and each tensor was fit with an uncompressed CPD at the selected rank.
Components of each alternative fit were matched to the expression-product fit by Hungarian matching and their mean absolute cosine over the condition and LR pair modes was computed.

### Significance Against Nulls

We extended the cluster-label permutation of CellPhoneDB and CellChat to continuous eigen-states\ [@doi:10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9; @doi:10.1038/s41596-020-0292-x].
Within each condition, the rows of the projection matrix $P_{i}$ were shuffled, permuting which cell was paired with each projection row, and the communication tensor was recomputed from the uncompressed RISE fit.
This was repeated for 1,000 permutations.
For each tensor entry, an empirical one-sided p-value was computed against the permuted scores.

Following scDiffCom, we tested whether each LR pair's per-sample score (computed as for individual LR pair associations, divided by the sample's total normalized expression) differed between patient groups\ [@doi:10.1038/s43587-023-00514-x].
The test statistic was the difference in mean score between two groups.
The null was formed by 10,000 permutations of outcome labels between patients, moving samples from the same patient together.
Empirical one-sided p-values were computed and corrected across the component's top 10 LR pairs.
For volcano plots, the effect size of each component's top 20 LR pairs was the log~2~ ratio of the two groups' mean scores.

### External Biological Validation

**NicheNet downstream-target validation.** We tested whether each component's receiver cells upregulated the downstream gene targets of the component's ligands using the NicheNet v2 ligand--gene-target database\ [@doi:10.1038/s41592-019-0667-5; @doi:10.1038/s41596-024-01121-9].
For each CPD component, NicheNet scores were computed as follows.
First, receiver cell types were defined as those whose mean per-cell receiver weight was at least 0.4 times that of the top cell type.
Per-gene scores were then computed for genes detected in at least 10% of cells of either group by a Wilcoxon rank-sum test between cells above the 90th percentile of receiver weight within those cell types (top receivers) and the remaining cells below the 10th percentile of receiver weight (bottom receivers).
To correct for hub genes linked to many ligands, each ligand's top 250 targets in the NicheNet database were weighted by $\log(N_{L}/n_{t})$, where $N_{L}$ is the number of ligands in the prior and $n_{t}$ the number of ligands listing target $t$.
Each ligand was scored by the AUROC with which the Wilcoxon statistics ranked its NicheNet targets above non-targets.
Target scores were averaged across ligands and weighted by each ligand's loading (the norm of the LR pair loadings ($G$) of its LR pairs), resulting in a summary NicheNet score per component.
A null was formed by permuting the top and bottom receiver labels among those cells 1,000 times, preserving group sizes, and repeating the DE test, gene filter, target scoring, and weighted mean on each permutation.
Only ligands scored on every permutation entered the observed and null weighted means.
Finally, an empirical one-sided p-value was computed for each component and corrected across components.

**NICHES concordance.** We tested whether the cells CCC-RISE assigns to a component signal through the component's LR pairs in their own expression by using NICHES\ [@doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btac775].
For each CPD component, with sender, receiver, and LR pair loadings $e$, $f$, and $g$ (its columns of $E$, $F$, and $G$), the sender population was the cells whose per-cell sender weight was at least $\tau = 0.3$ times its largest value, $(Pe)_{j} \geq \tau \max_{j'}(Pe)_{j'}$, and the receiver population was defined similarly by $(Pf)_{j} \geq \tau \max_{j'}(Pf)_{j'}$.
Unlike the label-free groups (below), which give each cell one role, a cell past both cutoffs belonged to both populations.
The component's carrying pairs, $\mathcal{C}$, were the fewest LR pairs, taken in order of $\left| g_{l} \right|$, that carried 90% of $\sum_{l} g_{l}^{2}$, up to 10.
NICHES was run on each sample's cells using CCC-RISE's normalized expression.
CellToSystem scored each cell as a sender, as its ligand expression times the mean receptor expression of all cells in its sample, and SystemToCell scored it as a receiver, as its receptor expression times the mean ligand expression of all cells in its sample.
Cells that were the only one of their coarse cell type in their sample were not scored by NICHES and were excluded (25 ALAD and 10 IBD cells).
Cell $j$'s program score on each side was $n_{j} = \sum_{l \in \mathcal{C}} g_{l}^{2}s_{jl}$, where $s_{jl}$ is its NICHES score for LR pair $l$, and cells with $n_{j} > 0$ were deemed NICHES-positive.
A population's NICHES concordance was the fraction of its cells that were NICHES-positive.

Each population's concordance was compared with two references.
The first was the concordance its cell-type labels predict: the mean, over the population's cells, of the fraction of NICHES-positive cells in each cell's fine cell type (or lineage).
The second replaced the component's loadings with random directions in eigen-state space, wherein a null was computed as follows.
First, each of 1,000 directions $u$ was drawn uniformly from the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^{r}$, and each cell's score became $(Pu)_{j}$ in place of $(Pe)_{j}$ or $(Pf)_{j}$.
From each fine cell type, the cells with the largest scores were taken, as many as the population held from that type.
The concordance of these cells formed the null distribution.
Empirical one-sided p-values against the 1,000 directions were corrected across each cohort's populations.
To show what concordance depends on, all cells were also ranked by five orderings and the population's number of top-ranked cells taken from each: a random direction ($Pu$, not matched for cell type), the per-cell weight, the positive part of each of these multiplied by the cell's ligand (senders) or receptor (receivers) expression, and that expression alone.
For the two orderings using random directions, concordance was the median over 200 directions.
This expression was the cell's centered expression of the ligands or receptors of all the component's LR pairs, each gene weighted by the squared LR pair loadings $g_{l}^{2}$ of its pairs.

### Mapping CCC-RISE Components to Cells

**Per-cell sender and receiver weights.** Because each cell's projection onto the eigen-states is retained in $P_{i}$, CPD eigen-state factors can be mapped back to individual cells.
The per-cell sender and receiver weights of all cells are $P \cdot E$ and $P \cdot F$, respectively, where $P$ stacks the projection matrices $P_{i}$ of all conditions by row and $E$ and $F$ are the sender and receiver eigen-state factors, respectively.
The agreement of a component's sender and receiver cells was summarized by the R^2^ between per-cell sender and receiver weights across all cells.
Components were mapped to annotated cell types by the mean per-cell sender and receiver weight of each broad cell type.

**Label-free sender and receiver groups.** To interpret a component without cell-type labels, each cell's per-cell sender and receiver weights were divided by their respective maxima across cells.
Cells for which either ratio was at least $\tau = 0.3$ formed the sender or receiver group, assigned to the role with the larger ratio.
Groups were compared by differential gene expression.
For ALAD analyses, marker genes were curated from Travaglini et al.\ and Sikkema et al.\ [@doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2922-4; @doi:10.1038/s41591-023-02327-2].
Sender and receiver groups were compared for curated genes, p-values were corrected across candidate markers present in the data, and markers were reported if q < 0.05 and the difference in the fraction of cells detecting the gene was at least 0.2.
Each group was also compared with all other cells, with correction across all genes.

**Label-free groups across components.** As above, per-cell weights in each component were divided by their respective maxima across cells.
Based on these relative weights, a polar magnitude and angle were computed for each cell with angles ranging from 0--90° between components.
Cells were thresholded by magnitude 0.3, and those above that threshold were partitioned into groups by angle: 0--30°, 30--60°, and 60--90°.
Groups were compared by differential gene expression.
For IBD analyses, marker genes were curated from Beumer et al.\ (2018, 2020), Gehart et al., and Krzak et al.\ [@doi:10.1038/s41556-018-0143-y; @doi:10.1016/j.cell.2020.04.036; @doi:10.1016/j.cell.2018.12.029; @doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02634-7].
Groups were compared for curated genes, p-values were corrected across candidate markers present in the data, and markers were reported if q < 0.05 and the difference in the fraction of cells detecting the gene was at least 0.2.

### Cell Type Composition

Cell type composition was analyzed by calculating the fraction of each sample's cells belonging to each broad cell type.
Fractions were compared across sample groups by Kruskal--Wallis tests, with correction across cell types.

### Comparator Methods

**Common inputs.** Each comparator used CCC-RISE's normalized expression and LR pairs, with complexes taken as the minimum over their subunits.
Cells were pooled by sample and annotated cell type at two levels of annotation: coarse (8 ALAD broad cell types and 7 IBD lineages) and fine (26 ALAD and 54 IBD cell types).
Each tensor had modes sample, sender cell type, receiver cell type, and LR pair.
We call one column of a fit's LR pair factor an LR column.
For CPD fits, an LR column belongs to one component, which gives it condition, sender, and receiver loadings.
For STACCato, each LR column's condition, sender, and receiver loadings were the leading left singular vectors of its core slice unfolded along each of those modes, mapped through the factor matrices of those modes.

**Pseudobulk CPD.** Each entry was the product of mean ligand expression in the sender and mean receptor expression in the receiver, with cell types absent from a sample set to zero.
CPD was fit and its rank selected as described in Canonical Polyadic Decomposition and Rank Selection, from agreement between starts and collinearity in the LR pair mode, so pseudobulk CPD differed from CCC-RISE only in the tensor it decomposed.
Ranks were swept up to 25 (ALAD fine) and 20 (IBD fine), and up to the number of cell types on coarse labels.
Ranks were 4 (coarse) and 5 (fine) on ALAD, and 6 and 5 on IBD, and the reported fit was the best start of $f_{\max}$.

**Tensor-cell2cell.** Each gene's expression was the fraction of a cell type's cells detecting it, and each entry was the mean of the ligand and receptor values\ [@doi:10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2].
Non-negative CPD was fit from 10 random starts at each rank up to 25 (coarse) and 20 (fine) on ALAD and 15 on IBD, and the rank was taken at the Kneedle elbow of the mean error.
Ranks were 8 and 6 on ALAD and 3 and 3 on IBD, and the reported fit was the lowest-error start at that rank.
We departed from the published analysis in four ways, each meant to let the method perform at its best; masking and keeping the best start are both options of the method's software.
The published analysis kept only cell types present in every sample, which here would drop 5 of 8 coarse and 18 of 26 fine ALAD labels and 1 of 7 and 50 of 54 IBD labels (84%, 89%, 25%, and 99% of observed entries), so we kept every cell type and masked absent entries.
The rank came from Kneedle rather than by eye, fits ran for up to 1,000 iterations at a tolerance of 10^−12^ rather than 100 at 10^−6^, and we kept the best of the starts.

**STACCato.** Entries were pseudobulk products with the default filters of LIANA, as in the authors' pipeline: an LR pair scored zero where its ligand or receptor was detected in under 10% of the sender's or receiver's cells, or where either cell type had under 5 cells in the sample\ [@doi:10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.05.005; @doi:10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0].
We kept every cell type, where the authors keep those present in at least 80% of samples, and set absent entries to zero.
An unsupervised Tucker decomposition, without a sample covariate, was fit with a Python re-implementation of the authors' algorithm, using the default stopping settings of the authors' paper and code.
On the same input tensors, the re-implementation matched the authors' R scripts numerically.
Each mode kept the components with more than 1% of the eigenvalue share of its unfolding, giving 16 and 14 LR columns on ALAD and 5 and 12 on IBD.

**Comparing components and LR columns.** The match between a CCC-RISE component and an LR column was the squared cosine (cos^2^) of their LR pair loadings over CCC-RISE's LR pairs.
Containment was the share of a unit LR column's squared norm in the span of all of another fit's LR columns, computed by QR projection.
A column was contained at a value of at least 0.85 and above the 95th percentile of 1,000 row permutations of the span, which accounts for span size.
A column's effective LR pairs were the inverse Simpson index of its squared loadings, $\left( \sum_{l} x_{l}^{2} \right)^{2}/\sum_{l} x_{l}^{4}$, so that $k$ equal loadings give $k$.
A column's homophilic share was the share of its squared loading on LR pairs whose ligand and receptor are the same gene.
Carrying pairs were defined as for NICHES concordance.
Coarse and fine LR columns of a method were joined where their cos^2^ was at least 0.09.

**Column classes.** Each comparator LR column took the first class it met, in order:

1. same as a CCC-RISE program: contained in CCC-RISE's LR pair span;
2. part of a CCC-RISE program: at least half of its squared loading on one component's carrying pairs;
3. broad: at least 20 effective LR pairs;
4. homophilic adhesion: homophilic share of at least 0.8;
5. single pair: fewer than 1.5 effective LR pairs;
6. mixed pairs: everything else.

No column had between 8.5 and 27.9 effective LR pairs, so the broad cutoff sits in an empty range.

**Label ceiling.** For each component and side, the label ceiling was the per-cell weight R^2^: the share of variance in its per-cell weights held by means over sample and label, the most that any method pooling cells by sample and annotation could represent.
For each labeling, it was compared with the closest pseudobulk CPD or STACCato column by LR pair cos^2^, painted on cells as the cell's sample loading times its cell-type loading, as the squared correlation of that value with the per-cell weight.

**Pairs in STACCato's columns.** Each carrying pair of a component was assigned to the STACCato column with its largest squared loading, and a column's share of the component was the summed share of the component's squared loading over the LR pairs assigned to it.
Columns carrying at least 10% of a component were tested for co-variation.

**Co-variation across methods.** The co-variation test of individual LR pair associations was extended to every component and LR column.
LR pairs were scored in each component's own context on its own method's tensor, weighting that tensor by the component's sender and receiver loadings as in $S_{il}$, and each component's carrying pairs were tested in place of its top 10 LR pairs.
The statistic was the mean pairwise Spearman correlation across samples, $\bar{\rho}$, compared with 2,000 random and 2,000 expression-matched draws; a component passed when $\bar{\rho}$ exceeded the larger of the two 95th percentiles, the stricter null.
The test was repeated over gene-disjoint pairs of LR pairs only, dropping pairs that share any gene from the statistic and from each draw, and a component with no such pairs could not be tested.
Components and columns with fewer than two carrying pairs could not be tested at all (IBD components 2, 3, 4, and 6), and the supplementary summary omits columns whose top LR pair carries at least 0.8 of the squared loading, which leaves that pair little to co-vary with.
These are percentile thresholds and not corrected tests.

**Detection depth.** A sample's detection depth was its median number of genes detected per cell.
Depth tracking was the absolute Spearman correlation across samples between a component's absolute condition loadings and detection depth.
Per-cell normalization rescales counts but not which genes are detected, so detection depth is distinct from the sequencing depth that normalization removes.

**Association testing.** Comparator condition loadings were tested as in Component--outcome Association, with p-values corrected across all groupings and components within each fit.

**NicheNet on comparator columns.** Comparator LR columns of ALAD were tested as in NicheNet downstream-target validation, except for the choice of cells.
A column has one receiver value per label, so no cells can be taken within a label.
High cells were all cells of labels with a receiver loading of at least 0.4 times the largest, and low cells came from the lowest labels, added until they held at least 10% of cells.
Where every label cleared this cutoff, the column named no receiver, and the top labels, added until they held at least 10% of cells, were taken as high (9 Tensor-cell2cell columns).
Each CCC-RISE component was compared with the comparator LR columns carrying its LR pairs.
CCC-RISE components kept their top and bottom receivers.
Besides the cell shuffle, each column was tested against 1,000 copies of the prior with its ligand--target links reassigned, scoring each ligand as a percentile among the ligands scored on the same ranking and averaging these with the ligand weights.
p-values were corrected across the columns of each fit, and effects were reported as the observed weighted target score minus its mean over shuffled cells.

**Flow panels.** ALAD component 5's sender and receiver cells were its label-free sender and receiver groups among the cells labeled lung epithelium.
IBD EE cells were grouped by enteroendocrine state, and an EE cell was a component 3 or 4 sender where its relative sender weight was at least 0.3.
EC and tuft cells were component 3 and 4 receivers where their per-cell receiver weight was at least 0.3 times its largest value.
STACCato has one value per label, so its bands span the whole label.

### Batch, Patient, and Technical Variation

RISE does not explicitly remove batch effects, but its structure isolates sample-level variation.
Each sample is projected by its own projection matrix onto eigen-states shared across samples, so variation in how strongly a sample expresses a program is carried by its condition loading rather than distorting the shared eigen-state definitions; the eigen-states themselves are estimated from structure common across samples.
Technical variation that acts uniformly on a sample (e.g., sequencing depth, capture efficiency) is therefore expressed as a condition-factor offset, so we test associations on the condition factor with the sample as the unit of analysis rather than the cell.

Technical variation was also explicitly handled by the following.
Slice normalization prevented samples with many or highly variable cells from dominating the shared eigen-states.
The total-expression correction removed sample-wide scaling of the condition loadings before association testing.
A recipient's samples were kept together in the jackknife and in outcome-label permutations.

### Quantification and Statistical Analysis

Figure captions detail pertinent statistical analyses or metrics, the number of conditions, and confidence interval values.
Shared metrics are defined below.

**Hungarian matching of components.** Because component order and sign are not fixed, the components of two fits of the same rank were matched one-to-one by the assignment maximizing the summed similarity of matched pairs (Hungarian algorithm)\ [@doi:10.1002/nav.3800020109].
Unless stated otherwise, the similarity of a pair was its FMS over the compared modes.

**Benjamini--Hochberg multiple-test correction.** p-values were corrected for multiple testing by the Benjamini--Hochberg procedure across the family of tests stated with each analysis and corrected values were reported as q, with q < 0.05 considered significant\ [@doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x].

**Differential gene expression.** Two groups of cells were compared gene by gene with two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests on normalized expression of all cells in each group, using scanpy without tie correction\ [@doi:10.1186/s13059-017-1382-0].
A gene's detection rate in a group was the fraction of the group's cells with nonzero expression.
Where stated, genes were prefiltered or reported by their detection rate.
